Subject: Severe latency & 500s from APAC region - urgent

Evelyn —

We started seeing a sharp rise in tail latency (p95 -> 3.4s) and a flurry of 5xx errors for our APAC traffic around 20:45 UTC. This is impacting realtime features for our customers in APAC (chat & autocomplete). Traffic to other regions looks normal.

Things we've done on our side: restarted our API gateway, validated client SDK retries, and dropped concurrency to minimum. Error rate spikes coincide with sustained token throughput ~180k/min.

Attached is a small log snippet and a sampling of request/response headers. Can Redwood confirm whether there is regional throttling, queue backs, or a degraded AZ? We need immediate guidance — if a cross-region failover or wholesale routing change is available, we want to authorize it.

Please escalate to engineering and leadership if needed. This is P0 for our customers.

Thanks,
Jordan

Subject: Re: Fwd: Bridgehead APAC P0 — need routing fallback and exec visibility

Eve / team —

Thanks for the flag. Quick notes from SRE triage:
- Root indicators: allocator throttle counts on APAC az-2 are high and we're seeing persistent KV cache saturation for large-context sessions. That combination is driving queue delays and a small but growing 5xx population (~3.1% of requests).
- Current capacity headroom in APAC is low; automated failover did not trigger because a portion of the fleet is still reporting healthy L7 checks.

Immediate mitigation plan (recommended order):
1) Manual traffic steering: flip routing policy to prefer EU for new sessions for Bridgehead's VIP (no DNS TTL change required; use per-route override).
2) Enable conservative connection draining for APAC az-2 to preserve in-flight sessions but prevent new allocations.
3) Backfill hot spare capacity from EU reserved pool (we can preempt noncritical background jobs). Requires sign-off for prioritized burst — Aditya please confirm.
4) Apply a short-term KV cache admission control to drop largest contexts temporarily (few customers only) — this reduces max memory churn and improves queue tail.

We can have a playbook-driven fallback live within ~12–18 minutes after sign-off for the routing change. I'll attach the cross-region failover playbook and a concise runbook.

If leadership wants to be looped directly: we should notify Product & Sales for credit/SLAs.

— Hannah
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Jordan —

Short update and next steps: we executed the manual routing preference at 21:12 UTC (new session preference to EU for your VIP). Early metrics show p95 dropping toward baseline for new sessions and 5xx rate falling from 3.1% -> 0.6% over ~45 minutes. We also enabled conservative connection drain on APAC az-2 and kicked off a cache admission-control policy for the most memory-heavy contexts.

Operational summary (for your team and our execs):
- Timeline:
  • 20:40 UTC — APAC queue latency and 5xx spike begins
  • 21:12 UTC — manual routing preference applied (EU) for new sessions
  • 21:20–22:10 UTC — backfill capacity and drains in progress; gradual recovery
  • 22:05 UTC onward — customer-visible error rate declined; tail latency improving

- Current status: stable. Residual errors are under 1% and we are continuing to monitor for cache thrash. Our engineering team will keep the EU preference for new sessions for the next 4 hours and then re-evaluate.

- Impact & ask: We believe the root cause is allocator pressure + KV cache saturation when large-context workloads concentrate on az-2. We're planning a targeted capacity rebalance and a long-term fix in the runtime to better cap large-context admission.

Aditya and Marissa — next steps for leadership: please advise on whether we should proactively offer a service credit to Bridgehead for the 30–60 minute customer impact window (HS-431277). I have included a short postmortem checklist in the linked Jira ticket.

Jordan — sorry again for the interruption. We'll keep you posted with a short postmortem and the timeline for the mitigation work. If you want immediate rollback (restore APAC preference), say the word and we'll coordinate; otherwise we'll let EU preference continue for the short window.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
